A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynCL, and their supplied text, equations, figures and tables are readable. However, v3 references Appendix B.1 for runtime analysis, which is absent from the supplied PDF. Neither supplied file contains appendices, limiting comparison of that referenced material.

before.justification: v2 reports original nuScenes tracking and detection experiments, component and matching ablations, hyperparameter studies, and training-cost measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and reports additional StreamPETR, nuScenes test-set, matching-ablation and inference-speed results.

M1.justification: Equation 11 adds temperature scaling of kernel similarities by tau, revising the reported contrastive objective; v2 has no temperature factor. The parallel decoders, hybrid assignments and contrastive architecture remain intact. Renaming Cost-based Query Filtering to Dynamic Query Filtering does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate camera-based 3D tracking and detection on nuScenes, with the same category coverage. The additional test split and detector configurations change evaluation settings, not the represented dataset, domain or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 newly includes OneTrack in validation and test comparisons, and STAR-Track and DORT in the test comparison. The ADA-Track comparison is updated to ADA-Track++, while the Past-reasoning-disabled PF-Track-F control is removed. PF-Track-S and TBA-Baseline persist under the names PF-Track and Baseline#1.

E3.justification: v3 adds nuScenes test-set evaluation, StreamPETR configurations at 320 × 800 and 640 × 1600, and FPS reporting with a stated single-A100, image-to-tracking timing boundary. It documents pretrained initialization and sliding-window training for the new StreamPETR baseline. Newly disclosed epoch schedules do not establish changed budgets for retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 becomes v3 Table 5: the C-decoder persistent-GT one-to-one condition is removed, and a C-decoder newborn-GT one-to-many condition is added. The standard baseline is redisplayed. Figure 5 replaces the full-resolution PF-Track cost comparison with Baseline#2. Component, filtering-method and hyperparameter studies otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. Experimental tables continue to present point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds SynCL StreamPETR AMOTA results of 51.8% and 58.9%, plus 58.8% on the test set. Its 50.7% full-resolution PETR entry replaces v2's 48.5%, but matching Past-reasoning settings are not established. CC-3DT validation AMOTA changes from 41.0% to 42.9%; the S-decoder one-to-many ablation's NDS/mAP changes from 47.7%/38.8% to 46.5%/37.1%. FPS results are added and some comparator detection scores disappear. The first three paired baseline comparisons retain their scores.

T1.justification: Equation 10 replaces v2's density-maximization expression with a negative log-likelihood summed over matching costs, explicitly including mixture weights among fitted parameters. v3 also formally identifies the reliable cluster through its lower mean. This revises the mathematical formulation; the remaining kernel derivation is retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim self-attention causes the identified optimization difficulties, propose a broadly compatible synergistic training strategy, and claim improved tracking and detection without inference overhead. Both already claim state-of-the-art performance in their conclusions. v3's 58.9% abstract headline updates supporting results rather than introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets improved recall without substantial false-positive growth as evidence of better candidate selection. Its matching discussion replaces the explanation of weak one-to-one assignment with an explanation based on reduced newborn-only supervision. It also removes v2's statement that the design maintains the total parameter count.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands implementation documentation with 12/24-epoch schedules by resolution, eight A100 GPUs, batch size 1, explicit backbone/resolution columns, StreamPETR initialization and training details, and FPS measurement conditions. It clarifies discarding contrastive parameters at inference. These are disclosures, not proof that retained experiments changed. Code remains a future-release promise, and no temperature value is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds TQD-Track discussion, DORT and ADA-Track++ references, and contrastive-learning context citing Chen et al. (2021), Caron et al. (2021) and Wu et al. (2018). The central positioning around general joint detection-and-tracking optimization remains unchanged; citation-style conversion is editorial.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the attention explanation into two explicit cases, revises Sections 3.4–3.5, renames the filtering module, and reorganizes experimental discussion into generality, state-of-the-art comparison and cost analysis. Related-work headings and contribution formatting change, while the overall five-section narrative remains.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is rearranged, Figure 2 separates the attention map from prediction panels, and Figure 4 is revised. Validation comparisons are separated, a test table is added, and old Tables 2–3 are merged into Table 4. Backbone, resolution and FPS columns substantially alter the displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 provides broader detector and baseline validation, held-out test results, inference-speed evidence and substantially clearer training documentation. The revised GMM formulation also improves precision. These strengthen assessment of the existing contribution, although the missing runtime appendix, unspecified temperature and removal of one matching control leave material gaps.
